newsitem.title: FRANCE: France shoots down Europe resolution om immigrants.
newsitem.headline: France shoots down Europe resolution om immigrants.

text.p: France on Wednesday rejected a resolution by the Council of Europe's parliament which advocates a smaller role for national parliaments in dealing with immigration policies.

Michel Barnier, junior minister for European Affairs, told France's National Assembly (lower house) during weekly questions that the text of the resolution approved on September 27 was "absurd and demagogical".

"As far as controlling immigration is concerned, the government will continue its policy...with unchanged rigour, humanity and determination," he said, adding that the resolution had been approved by 171 European deputies out of a total of 626.

The declaration by the Council's assembly which safeguards human rights and democracy in Europe, had urged its 39 member states to step up the fight against racism and improve the legal situation of immigrants.
It also suggested that governments reach bilateral agreements with immigrant countries that would help contain illegal immigration and encourage foreigners to return home.
"The Europeanisation of the issue (of immigration) entails the exclusion of national parliaments," the text said.
The European vote on the resolution was passed despite a move by French centrist and right-wing deputies to block it.
France's centre-right government has taken a tough stance on immigration and Prime Minister Alain Juppe last month announced that he was further stiffening laws on illegal immigration.
